newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN seeks $33 mln for 300,000 Angolan refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN seeks $33 mln for 300,000 Angolan refugees.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency appealed on Friday for $33.6 million to help settle more than 300,000 Angolan refugees expected to return home, saying the lack of funding may force it to suspend or sharply cut its programme.
"...the slow movement toward political normalcy in Angola has dampened donor interest," the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said in a blunt statement.
The Geneva-based agency, which supplies returnees with shelter materials, seeds, tools and food, has received only $4.6 million from donors after its February appeal for $38.2 million.
The renewed appeal comes as the Angolan army pushes deeper into diamond-rich areas held by the UNITA opposition in the northeast, displacing thousands.

"The return of the refugees is a key component of the peace process. Our inability to bring about repatriation may set back the timetable for peace," Nicolas Bwakira, UNHCR's regional director for southern Africa, was quoted as saying.
"Because of the slow donor response we will now have to consider closing down field offices in Angola," he added.
Angolan government forces and UNITA signed a peace treaty in 1994 to end a 20-year civil war which claimed 600,000 lives and forced three million from their homes.

Nearly 93,000 Angolan refugees have returned home on their own since 1995. Some 200,000 remain in the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, 96,000 in Zambia, 12,000 in Congo and 1,000 in Namibia. Another 15,000 are in 32 other countries.

Another U.N. agency, the World Food Programme (WFP), told a news briefing in Geneva that on Saturday it would airlift emergency food supplies for one month to Nzage in the northeast, where 3,500 people displaced by fighting have settled.

The Luanda government said its military operation was intended to flush out armed refugees who had come across the border from the Democratic Republic of Congo, but analysts said this was a pretext to retake diamond-rich areas held by the UNITA opposition.
